analysis.title: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS): 3Q26 Key Takeaways: Big earnings reset sends shares lower
key_insights: GS says FIS's large cut to forward guidance will likely be a near-term overhang until the CFO transition is complete. GS's view is that management pulled an earnings reset forward alongside the CFO transition to de-risk the outlook while the search is underway.

Management described the updated outlook as containing a number of 'prudent' assumptions. GS believes the sticky nature of the business and strong free cash flow generation will continue to anchor valuation, despite another setback in building predictability.
GS thinks the qualitative commentary on the drivers of the cut was less clear. It expects this to raise investor questions about the full extent of the issues in the near term.

GS wants more detail on three items: the nature of implementation delays across large clients, the 2027 margin outlook and persistence of cyber-related tech spending, and the strategic review process and its effect on leverage and the path to capital return.

GS expects the prudent revenue assumptions and recurring revenue growth (trending at 3% in banking and 5% in capital markets) to help FIS return to its long-term compounder record and more normalized multiples. FIS trades at about 6x GS 2027 EPS and about 8x GS 2027 GAAP free cash flow.
GS notes that actions from the strategic review of non-core businesses could have strategic merit.
3Q26 segment revenue was about $3.371bn versus consensus of $3.356bn. Adjusted EBITDA from consolidated FIS segments was $1.482bn versus consensus of $1.472bn (Visible Alpha).
Banking Solutions 3Q26 revenue was $2.548bn (+41% on an adjusted basis) versus consensus of $2.539bn. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.208bn at a 47.4% margin versus $1.178bn and 46.4% expected.
Capital Markets 3Q26 revenue was $823mn (+3% adjusted), 1% above consensus. Adjusted EBITDA was $444mn at a 54.0% margin versus $430mn and 52.6% expected.

FY26 guidance was lowered: revenue $13.445-13.505bn, adjusted EBITDA $5.565-5.605bn (41.4%-41.5% margin), adjusted EPS $5.82-5.89. 4Q26 guidance is revenue $3.319-3.379bn, adjusted EBITDA $1.370-1.410bn, adjusted EPS $1.37-1.40.
Preliminary FY27 guidance: Banking Solutions growth flat to 1.5%, Capital Markets -1.5% to 0.5%, margin change of -100bps to 0bps, and a low-double-digit to high-single-digit decline in EPS.

GS cut its price target to $35 from $44, based on about 6.5x P/E (about 7x previously, citing higher competition) applied to Q5-Q8 EPS. Rating is Buy, with 17.6% upside from the $29.76 close on 4 Nov 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut on lower guidance and estimates and a lower P/E multiple (about 6.5x versus about 7x) on higher competition. GS keeps the Buy, citing sticky revenue and strong free cash flow.

tension_points.bull_case: GS argues the reset de-risks the outlook, the business is sticky, and strong free cash flow anchors valuation. FIS trades at about 6x 2027 EPS and about 8x 2027 GAAP free cash flow, and recurring revenue is growing 3% in banking and 5% in capital markets.
tension_points.bear_case: The qualitative commentary on the drivers of the cut was less clear, which may raise investor questions about the full extent of the issues. The cut is another setback in building predictability, and the CFO transition adds an overhang.
